significance.root_decision: All five assertions of Conjecture 3.4 of Wang and Zhao hold: for a prime p exceeding the weight plus one, every r >= 1 and every exponent vector s of positive integers, the finite sums Z_{p^r}^{d}(s) over compositions of p^r into d positive parts prime to p satisfy the stated divisibility by powers of p, the scaling laws in depths 4 and 5 relating level p^{r+1} to level p^r, and the general recurrence in r. Earlier work (Chen and Zhao; McCoy, Thielen, Wang and Zhao) treated only exponents all equal to 1, where just the last assertion applies; the source proved depth 3 by Bernoulli-number computations. The proof lifts the sum from level p^r to p^{r+1} keeping double precision (modulus p^{2r+1}), shows that the second moments of the carries vanish modulo p, and projects onto one reflection parity to gain a further factor of p. Lean states the sums and the five congruences literally in the integers modulo prime powers.
significance.caveat: Bounded literature search. The citing-paper check was completed in part by root and a second cross-model lane after the GPT-6.1 Sol final check had left eligibility in doubt: of the seven papers citing McCoy et al., the one that could overlap, Wang and Ma, arXiv:2511.23308 (2025), was read in full and treats only depth 3 with exponents (1, 1, 1), a case the source itself attributes to earlier work; Shen 2024 (doi 10.1155/2024/8445635) could be read only in abstract (triple reciprocal sums modulo p^2, r = 1). The list of papers citing the source itself could not be fetched (rate limits). Cross-model confidence: correct 0.85 (every step checked by hand, 660 brute-force cases), not routine 0.65, not public 0.95 for the papers read. The printed example for p = 13 is proved modulo 13^5; its sharpness modulo 13^6 is computed, not formalized. No second cross-model lane read the finished Lean: the statement file is byte-identical to the one that reviewer confirmed as literal.
